commitResults.messageTitle: Test duplicates with category case changes
commitResults.messageBody: Inventory category matching is case-insensitive, so differently cased category input must not bypass duplicate detection. Verify the error message and ensure the original stock remains unchanged.
An insufficient-stock error must leave the item quantity untouched. Verify both the diagnostic quantities and the inventory state after the rejected removal.
Conflicting sessions must not enter the schedule. Verify the reported conflict, retain the existing session, and confirm that no second session is added.
An out-of-range deletion must not remove another scheduled session. Verify the range-aware message and preserve the existing session after the failure.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test adjacent sessions do not conflict
commitResults.messageBody: Back-to-back sessions at the same location should be schedulable. Verify that a session ending as another begins is not treated as overlapping.

Inventory items can be mutated after insertion, allowing their identity or stock to become invalid. Make item identity immutable and expose only validated partial stock removal so stored inventory state remains consistent.
Inventory addition relies on an assertion that may be disabled in production. Enforce the public method contract unconditionally so null items fail before inventory state is inspected or changed.
Session scheduling relies on an assertion that is normally disabled. Enforce the public boundary unconditionally so invalid calls fail before logging or schedule mutation.
Automate console regression tests in CI

commitResults.messageTitle: fix: Exit cleanly when input closes
commitResults.messageBody: Console input can end without a Bye command, especially when redirected. Check for available lines before reading so startup and the command loop terminate without a NoSuchElementException.

An unexpected runtime failure during command dispatch can terminate the interactive application without useful diagnostics. Log the original cause at SEVERE and show a stable, nontechnical message so the user can continue.

Inventory mutations depend on categories and stored items remaining internally consistent. Assert after additions and removals that categories are nonblank and nonempty, items have positive stock and matching categories, and names remain unique within each category.

Schedule mutations rely on every stored session being present and mutually compatible. Assert after additions and deletions that the collection contains no null entries and no pair of conflicting sessions.

Preparation mutations rely on valid, accumulated requirements. Assert after additions and removals that entries are nonnull, names and categories are nonblank, quantities remain positive, and name-category pairs remain unique ignoring case.

regression cases to provide a baseline for the loan feature.

commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide describes session preparation in one short
paragraph without diagrams. Readers cannot see which classes own
the requirements or how they relate to inventory, and the Week 10
tP tasks require each member to document their feature's design.

Describe the responsibilities of each class, add a class diagram,

commitResults.messageTitle: Add item search across stock and loans
commitResults.messageBody:
Inventory shows only units in stock. When every unit of an item is
lent out, the item disappears from list-i, so a technician cannot
tell whether the lab still owns it without reading every loan.
Issue #40 asks for one lookup across all components.

Add ItemFinder, which matches a keyword against item names and
categories, ignoring case, and combines each item's stock with the
units on active loans. Each result is an immutable ItemLookupEntry
with a status of Available or All on loan.

Read stock through new Inventory#getItemSnapshots copies, so a
search cannot change inventory. Keep the matching in ItemFinder
rather than Parser so it can be tested without console output.

Issue #40 also mentions location, but inventory items do not store
one. Adding it would change add-i and the existing inventory model,
so leave it out of this iteration.

Validated with Java 25: ./gradlew check and the console regression
test pass.

Part of #40.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The class diagram shows how preparation is structured, but not how
a command flows through the classes at run time. Two behaviours
also surprise new readers. q/ means units per attendee for add-p
but total units for delete-p. A shortage can appear or disappear
without any preparation command, because stock is read live.

Add a four-step walkthrough with a summary table, a sequence
diagram of a successful add-p, the failure paths, and how
shortfalls are calculated when the list is displayed.

The sequence diagram meets the Week 10 requirement for at least
one sequence diagram per member.

Part of #53.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Item search exists but users cannot reach it from the console.

Add find-i KEYWORD. The whole argument is the keyword, so names
with spaces such as "red led" can be searched. A missing keyword
shows the usage message, like other commands.

Display results through Ui rather than printing from Parser, as
loan tracking does, so formatting stays in one place. Number the
rows and show a message when nothing matches. List the command in
help under Inventory.

Add parser tests for exact output, padding, missing keywords and
unchanged stock. Add four find-i commands to the console regression
test, and update the expected help output.

Validated with Java 25: ./gradlew check and the console regression
test pass.

Part of #40.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The preparation section explains what the feature does, but not
why it was designed this way. Without that, a reviewer cannot judge
the tradeoffs. For example, two sessions can both appear to have
enough stock because preparation never reserves it.

Compare the chosen design with an alternative for four aspects:
where requirements are stored, whether stock is reserved, storing
totals instead of per-attendee quantities, and how items are
identified. Summarise where each input is validated, which tests
cover it, and the known limitations.

The limitations note that listPreparation() prints from Parser
instead of Ui, which is a candidate for later cleanup.

Part of #53.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
